newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Placer set to break ground on disputed mine.
newsitem.headline: Placer set to break ground on disputed mine.

text.p: Minera La Cristinas (Minca), a joint venture between the Venezuelan government and Canada's Placer Dome Inc, on Saturday will officially start construction on the disputed $536 million Las Cristinas gold mine, Placer Dome said.
Four government ministers and several state company presidents will attend the ceremony in southeastern Venezuela, Placer said in a release issued Friday.

Placer, which has a 70 percent stake in Minca, is being challenged for the rights to Las Cristinas by Crystallex International Corp, which has introduced a claim for the rights to Cristinas 4 and 6 concessions with the Venezuelan Supreme Court.

Placer has estimated Las Cristinas' reserves at more than nine million ounces. Crystallex, which operates a small mine nearby, has said Las Cristinas could produce between 250,000 and 400,000 ounces of gold per year.
Venezuelan government officials have insisted throughout the dispute that Crystallex's claim is unjustified and that the joint venture in which Placer has a 70 percent stake will go ahead.
